name: Carolina Solar Energy III, LLC
old_description: An architect emeritus, building contractor, solar installer and real estate developer, Richard founded CSE in 2004. Through his leadership, CSE built the first utility-scale solar energy project in the Southeast in 2007. Richard is a lead policy advocate in NC for renewable energy and energy efficiency, past Chair of the NC Sustainable Energy Association and founder of the Carolinas Clean Energy Business Association.
about:
Carolina Solar Energy (CSE) was founded in 2004 in Durham, North Carolina, by Richard Harkrader, an architect emeritus, building contractor, and solar installer. The family-owned business began with a goal to demonstrate that renewable energy legislation could build a solar industry in the state. After years of trial and error, Harkrader completed the first utility-scale solar project in the Southeast at NC State University in 2007. Business partner Gerry Dudzik joined that same year, bringing permitting experience from the cellular tower industry. In 2012, Richard's daughter Carson Harkrader joined after a career at GE Energy, and she assumed leadership in 2018 when both founders retired.

The company develops utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) solar projects across the Southeast and Gulf South, with over 950 MWdc of projects operating or under construction. Its core services include site selection, interconnection applications, state permitting, landowner outreach, community relations, and policy advocacy. The team manages projects from early development through construction, collaborating with municipalities, utilities, and landowners. CSE also operates an intern program and has partnered with organizations like TROSA to provide workforce opportunities.

CSE serves utilities, municipal governments, and private landowners throughout North Carolina, Virginia, Kentucky, and Louisiana. Notable partners include the City of Raleigh, which completed its first major solar development with CSE, and Person County, which hosts three photovoltaic facilities totaling approximately five megawatts. The company focuses on bringing economic development to underserved areas and works with families who have managed land for generations.

CSE distinguishes itself through early-market entry and policy leadership. It was the first solar company to apply for Kentucky state-level permits in March 2020, and its advocacy work has helped shape renewable energy legislation in North Carolina. The firm emphasizes community acceptance, aiming to deliver projects that are welcomed by their host communities.
